question:
Five unit squares are arranged in the coordinate plane as shown, with the lower left corner at the origin. The slanted line, extending from \((a, 0)\) to \((3, 3),\) divides the entire region into two regions of equal area. What is \(a?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_12B_Q14_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The five unit squares have total area \(5\), so the shaded part must have area \(\frac52\). Completing this part to a triangle avoids calculating the pieces in individual squares.

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_12B_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

Add the missing unit square with vertices \((2,0)\), \((3,0)\), \((3,1)\), and \((2,1)\) to the shaded part. The resulting region is the right triangle with vertices \((a,0)\), \((3,0)\), and \((3,3)\). Thus its area is
\[
\frac52+1=\frac72.
\]
Its vertical height is \(3\), so the triangle area formula gives its horizontal base as
\[
\frac{2\cdot\frac72}{3}=\frac73.
\]
This base also has length \(3-a\). Therefore
\[
a=3-\frac73=\boxed{\frac23}.
\]
The result lies between \(0\) and \(1\), consistent with the intersection shown. The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

Gemini uses quadrant/axis features to assign coordinates in one diagram method. Coordinate differences and area can instead be computed from already supplied points without quadrant classification, so these features prepare rather than universally precede the task.

edges.reason: The criterion explicitly permits triangles OR rectangles. Preserve triangle area as a component of the triangular-piece route without making every composite-area task use it.
